Subject: SLO alignment and benchmarking next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on product fit. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the performance qualification we discussed: 

- Goals we heard: p99 latency target for conversational responses, sustained throughput to cover peak traffic, and correct behavior for streaming chunked outputs.
- Initial targets (please confirm): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 70ms, p99 <= 150ms for 20-token generations; steady-state throughput goal ~120 QPS; concurrency up to 250 active sessions.
- Streaming: client expects chunked server-side streaming for long responses (progressive token delivery) with per-chunk latency below ~50ms.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Benchmark spec (methodology, measurement definitions) — attached (redwood_bench_spec_v1.pdf).
- Example harness config we plan to run and a sanitized prompt set to validate reproducibility.
- A proposed benchmark window: 2 business days in a stable staging environment, then one-day replay on production-like infra.

Action items / next steps:
1) Samir: confirm the numeric SLOs above or send corrected targets.
2) Acme: share representative prompt set and a small sample of production latency traces if possible (we referenced a CSV template below).
3) Redwood: we will circulate the bench spec and schedule an engineer pairing session for streaming tests.

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (placeholder)

Looking forward — I’ll coordinate available slots for the pairing session.

Best,

Subject: Re: SLO alignment and benchmarking next steps

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and clarifying a few items from our side: 

- SLOs: agree on p50/p95/p99 bands but can we tighten p99 to 120ms for 20-token responses? That's what our UX team is pushing for.
- Throughput: the 120 QPS is our expected steady peak. We have occasional spikes to ~220 QPS during promotions; we'd like to see behavior up to that level.
- Concurrency: 250 active sessions is correct; many sessions are long-lived due to streaming.
- Streaming specifics: we expect chunked delivery with the first token within 100ms and subsequent chunks within ~50ms each. Also important: partial-response semantics — we must never send duplicated tokens across chunks.

I attached a small CSV with a few latency samples from our staging runs (acme_latency-sample.csv) to give you a baseline.

If you can confirm the methodology (how you measure p99 for streaming vs non-streaming), we can kick off the bench run next week.

—Samir

Subject: Re: SLO alignment and benchmarking next steps

Samir — perfect, thanks for the sample and the tighter p99 target. A few notes on methodology and what we will deliver so expectations are clear: 

Measurement definitions (high level) — full details in attached redwood_bench_spec_v1.pdf: 
- Non-streaming (complete-response): we measure end-to-end response time from request ingress at the load generator to final token commit into the wire (includes queuing and inference). Percentiles computed across all samples in the run window.
- Streaming: we capture both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for the first token and per-chunk inter-arrival latencies. For SLOs that map to p99, we report both p99(TTFB) and p99(inter-chunk). We also detect token duplication/loss by deterministic checks against ground-truth tokenization.
- Concurrency/throughput regimen: we will run stepped-load profiles — ramp to target concurrency, hold for observation windows (10 min), and then spike tests to the 220 QPS cap.
- Reproducibility: each bench will be run 3x with identical seeds and prompt sets; we version the harness and config. We will provide the harness config and a Docker image tag so you can reproduce locally.

Attachments: redwood_bench_spec_v1.pdf (bench methodology + measurement definitions)

Proposed schedule:
- Monday: share full harness config and bench spec (we did).
- Wednesday: engineer pairing for streaming tests (Ben will lead).
- Thursday-Friday: Redwood runs bench in staging; we share raw logs and summary metrics.

Ben, can you pick a two-hour slot on Wednesday afternoon for the pairing?

Olga
Olga Petro
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick technical note from the backend side — Samir, a couple specifics so expectations match our test harness: 

- Streaming profile: we will emulate chunked responses with 256-byte chunks and a configurable per-chunk delay. For the initial test we suggest 2s response length with 8 chunks (so chunk spacing ~250ms) but we can tighten to match your UX expectations.
- Concurrency test: our plan is to run 250 concurrent persistent connections for two separate 10-minute holds, and then run three 2-minute spike windows to 220 QPS.
- Measurement: p99 for inter-chunk latency will be computed across chunk events (not across sessions) and reported alongside p99 TTFB; logs will include sequence numbers so you can verify no duplicates.

I’ll include the harness command lines in the pairing session; happy to sync on any changes.

—Ben
